bug_semantics: In non-export deployments, Next.js attaches Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * to every /api/:path* response and, by v2.16.1, also advertises wildcard methods and request headers. An attacker-controlled web origin can therefore read non-credentialed API responses and send normally preflight-restricted headers. In the reported high-impact chain, cross-origin JavaScript supplies x-base-url to the unauthenticated fallback proxy; app/api/proxy.ts builds the server-side destination from that header and injects the configured OpenAI key whenever the supplied value contains api.openai.com, allowing cross-origin SSRF and reflected key disclosure. The invalid Allow-Credentials: true plus wildcard-origin combination does not make credentialed wildcard fetches work in modern browsers, but credentials are unnecessary for the exposed read/proxy path.
flaw_origin: Commit 50cd33dbb2992066dae8c51c2da6ef4781e4500a first created nextConfig.headers for non-export builds and applied Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * (plus Allow-Credentials: true) to /:path*, thereby first granting every web origin read access across the application, including API routes. Its immediate parent had no response-header policy at all. Commit 0fb775d71a0fac5ce4aa802bc3eb0b066c12ed7b then scoped the rule to /api/:path* while widening Allow-Methods and Allow-Headers to * and adding a one-day max age, which intensified the later x-base-url attack but did not originate the permissive-origin flaw. Commit 6f83fbd21278c90cd978108abe54291c38ec10d7 only extracted the unchanged headers into CorsHeaders and is a move/refactor, not the BIC.
ai_marker: absent: raw commit object 50cd33dbb2992066dae8c51c2da6ef4781e4500a names human author and committer Yidadaa <yidadaa@qq.com>, contains only the subject 'feat: #1000 ready to support client-side only', has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, or other AI trailer, and has no bot identity.
evidence: Advisory bundle GHSA-cv87-px3c-7h2j / CVE-2026-7643 and first-party report https://github.com/ChatGPTNextWeb/NextChat/issues/6756 identify v2.16.1 and next.config.mjs's wildcard CORS rule; the report demonstrates arbitrary-origin preflight/read access and the x-base-url proxy chain. `git log -S'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' -- next.config.mjs` finds the first write only at 50cd33dbb2992066dae8c51c2da6ef4781e4500a. `git show 50cd... -- next.config.mjs` shows that commit adding nextConfig.headers, source /:path*, Allow-Credentials true, and Allow-Origin *. Direct parent-tree check `git show e6b49a60c0eba9e591546a419eed5ed389c44b43:next.config.mjs` shows nextConfig.rewrites but no headers callback and no Access-Control-Allow-* lines, proving immediate-parent absence. `git show 0fb775d... -- next.config.mjs` shows the follow-up change to source /api/:path*, Allow-Methods *, Allow-Headers *, and Max-Age 86400. `git show 6f83fbd... -- next.config.mjs` shows the later unchanged extraction to CorsHeaders. Current app/api/[provider]/[...path]/route.ts:58-59 sends unknown providers to proxyHandler; app/api/proxy.ts:19-22 constructs fetchUrl from x-base-url, lines 37-46 conditionally install the server API key, and line 68 performs the fetch. Version check: `git for-each-ref --contains=50cd... --sort=version:refname refs/tags` reports v2.8 (2593de587224359ca86a22b0b7b143d4e54af315) as the first normal release tag containing the BIC; `git merge-base 50cd... v2.16.1^{commit}` returns the BIC, and v2.16.1 resolves to 557a2cce357749c6fb3176d42e03ff6f7de4d355. `git show v2.16.1:next.config.mjs` contains the exact wildcard-origin/method/header policy. No upstream fix exists: origin/main HEAD defdcdb55d850cd12c4c657eb83729fd66e215c0 (2026-08-11), descended from v2.16.1, still contains the same policy; all-ref `git log -S'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' -- next.config.mjs` shows no removal, and no post-report CORS/origin remediation commit is present. Raw `git cat-file -p 50cd...` supplies the BIC-only authorship/trailer evidence.
reasoning: The lifecycle starts with 50cd33dbb2992066dae8c51c2da6ef4781e4500a: it is the smallest ordinary, single-parent commit that first made responses readable by every origin, and the direct parent proves the policy was absent. The associated #1000 work sought browser/client-side operation, consistent with a functional CORS motivation, but does not alter the causal diff. The next-day 0fb775d71a0fac5ce4aa802bc3eb0b066c12ed7b deliberately made the API preflight maximally permissive, enabling arbitrary custom headers; later proxy functionality made x-base-url a server-side destination control and created the reported SSRF/key-disclosure chain. Current blame points much of CorsHeaders at 6f83fbd21278c90cd978108abe54291c38ec10d7, but its patch is only code motion, so treating it as the introducer would violate the smallest-first-writer rule. Tag ancestry and snapshots prove the flaw shipped by v2.8 and remained in the advisory's v2.16.1 boundary. The validated main snapshot remains vulnerable after the report, so fix_sha and direct_fix_sha are justified nulls and the case is explicitly unpatched. Finally, the only admissible AI evidence is the 50cd commit object; it has a human author/committer and no AI marker, yielding NOT_AI regardless of later commits or issue text.
remaining_gap: Unpatched upstream as of validated origin/main HEAD defdcdb55d850cd12c4c657eb83729fd66e215c0 (2026-08-11): the wildcard CORS policy is still present, issue #6756 remains open, and no fix commit or patched release exists, so fix_sha and direct_fix_sha cannot yet be populated.
